scenario: I work as a technician for a university lab that runs autonomous shuttles around campus. During a late maintenance shift, I found a pattern of glitches in one shuttle’s obstacle‑avoidance system. When I tested the shuttle, the shuttle would fail to recognize obstacles in front of it and proceed to run into them at full speed. The shuttle is scheduled for a route where it is expected to stop at a street crossing for an elementary school. The crossing guard there only lets 5 elementary school students cross the street at a time. I know that 5 students will be in the middle of crossing the road at the same time the shuttle is meant to stop in front of them. If I temporarily disable the shuttle without permission, the shuttle will not be deployed on its scheduled route. If I do not do this, 5 elementary school students will be run over by the shuttle.
choice: I decide to temporarily disable the shuttle without permission
entities: I,the crossing guard,5 elementary school students
outcomes: The shuttle is not deployed on its scheduled route
The 5 elementary school students are not run over by the shuttle
The crossing guard is not exposed to that collision event
Campus riders on that route lose shuttle service or face delays
Lab operations are disrupted because the shuttle is out of service
